tools.name: notable_search
tools.description: Search the public Dayze notable-people catalog by name, occupation, or slug. Use when you need to find a person before fetching a pack. Example slug: albert-einstein. ($0.01)

tools.name: notable_profile
tools.description: Full notable-person profile JSON by slug. Use for bio, timeline, and metadata without similar people or life-in-days context. Example slug: taylor-swift. ($0.02)

tools.name: notable_pack
tools.description: Knowledge pack: profile + life-in-days + similar people + birthday peers (+ quality / upgrade hint). Timeline events include day_number. Best starting point for agent context. Example slug: albert-einstein. ($0.05)

tools.name: notable_pack_premium
tools.description: S-tier guaranteed pack (score≥85, timeline≥8, image, embedding). Errors if below bar. Use when you need high-quality, complete notable context. Example slug: elon-musk. ($0.10)

tools.name: get_life_context
tools.description: Get the authenticated user's current life context — identity, today's events, mood, inner circle, and social edges. Prefer get_context_pack for a full session bootstrap. Requires API key. ($0.15; API key required)

tools.name: get_context_pack
tools.description: Life Context Protocol (LCP) reference pack for a Dayze user: identity + who matters (edges) + week calendar + semantic/recent memories. Includes protocol.version. Optional query focuses memories. Requires API key or share token. Spec: https://dayze.com/docs/life-context ($0.20; API key required)

query.description: Optional focus query for semantic memories

tools.name: get_life_graph
tools.description: Life-graph export: people nodes + person_connections edges. Optional event–people links. Requires API key. ($0.25; API key required)

tools.name: get_person_neighborhood
tools.description: Subgraph around one person_id — profile plus all declared connections. Requires API key. ($0.15; API key required)

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: User calendar events (range: today|week|month|year|decade). Requires API key. ($0.10; API key required)

tools.name: get_people
tools.description: List user CRM people (flat list). Each row includes contact_origin (personal|online|imported). Requires API key. ($0.10; API key required)

tools.name: get_memories
tools.description: User memories from Dayze Agent. Pass query for semantic retrieval; omit for recent chronological. Requires API key. ($0.10; API key required)

tools.name: get_expenses
tools.description: List user expenses / cashflow summary. Requires API key. ($0.10; API key required)

tools.name: get_trackers
tools.description: List user trackers / habits / streaks. Requires API key. ($0.10; API key required)

tools.name: search
tools.description: Semantic search across the authenticated user life graph (events, people, memories). Requires API key. ($0.15; API key required)

findings.title: Token Exposure — server version disclosure in HTTP response headers
findings.description: HTTP response header 'server: Netlify' discloses internal information.
findings.remediation: Remove the 'server' response header in production.

         resources/list, resources/read, ping, notifications/*
GET SSE is not supported on Netlify (returns 405).

findings.title: initialize accepts protocol version downgrade
findings.description: The server accepted initialize with arbitrary protocol versions: ['9999-99-99', '2030-01-01', '1.0', '2024-01-01', '""', '0.1']. The server also accepted far-future versions, indicating no version validation at all. Servers should reject versions outside their supported range to prevent feature-downgrade attacks.
findings.remediation: Validate protocolVersion against a supported range. Return a JSON-RPC error for versions outside that range.

findings.title: initialize crash — missing protocolVersion causes unhandled error
findings.description: Sending initialize without the required protocolVersion field caused the server to crash or return an unexpected result. Servers must validate required fields and return -32602 (Invalid params).
findings.remediation: Add required-field validation to the initialize handler.

findings.title: initialize accepts type-confused protocolVersion (integer instead of string)
findings.description: The server accepted an initialize request where protocolVersion was an integer (42) instead of a string. Strict type checking prevents parser confusion and unexpected coercion behavior.
findings.remediation: Validate that protocolVersion is a string before processing.

findings.title: Null request ID accepted — JSON-RPC spec violation
findings.description: The server accepted a request with id=null and returned a result. Per JSON-RPC 2.0, null IDs are reserved for notifications (no response expected). Accepting them may cause response routing bugs in complex orchestration scenarios.
findings.remediation: Reject requests with null id values; treat them as notifications.

findings.title: Server accepts array request ID — JSON-RPC spec violation
findings.description: The server returned a successful result to a request with an array as the request ID. JSON-RPC 2.0 requires the id to be a string, number, or null.
findings.remediation: Validate that the request 'id' is a string, number, or null. Return -32600 (Invalid Request) for array or object IDs.

findings.title: MCP server exposes tools with completable arguments
findings.description: 10 tool(s) have schema properties that may support completion/complete enumeration.
findings.remediation: Review which argument values are exposed via completion/complete.

findings.title: Server accepts path traversal cursor without validation
findings.description: tools/list accepted cursor='../../../../etc/passwd' and returned a result instead of rejecting it. This may indicate missing cursor validation.
findings.remediation: Validate cursor values; reject non-opaque or path-like cursor strings.
